title: The Teacup
rule: Make everything tiny, small enough to fit in a teacup.

title: From Above
rule: Look down on everything from straight overhead, the way a passing rook would see it.

title: Close Enough to Touch
rule: Come in so close that the subject spills off the edges of the page.

title: The Lantern
rule: Choose a single source of light and let it decide where every shadow goes.

title: The Moon
rule: Use nothing but a deep blue and White, as if the moon were the only light.

title: The Hearthfire
rule: Use warm colours only, and burnish them until they glow like embers.

title: The Sepia Hour
rule: Use only Dark Brown and White, on tan or kraft paper if you have some.

title: Three Pencils Only
rule: Use just the three pencils dealt, and make them do all the work.

title: Opposites
rule: Use the two opposite colours and nothing else, layering one over the other for the shadows.

title: The Postage Stamp
rule: Shrink the picture to the size of a postage stamp, with a perforated edge all round.
phrases: a scene the size of a thumbnail

title: Seen Through Glass
rule: Put a pane of glass between you and the scene, and show it with one streak of reflection.
phrases: a faint double of the room

title: Half Hidden
rule: Tuck half of the subject behind something nearer, and let the visible half tell the story.

title: The Keyhole
rule: Frame the scene inside a keyhole shape, as though you were peering through an old door.

title: The Visitor
rule: Hide a small animal somewhere in the picture for someone else to find.

title: One Long Line
rule: Draw the outline in one long line without lifting the pencil, then colour as usual.

title: Left Hand Warm-Up
rule: Work with the hand you don't write with for the first five minutes, then swap back.

title: The Mirror
rule: Bring back an old friend from your sealed cards and draw it again at a new hour.

title: Three Studies
rule: Draw the subject three times across the page, from the front, the side and the back.

title: The Bookmark
rule: Fit everything into a tall, narrow strip the shape of a bookmark.

title: The Single Skein
rule: Keep to one colour family only, in a light, a middle and a dark.
phrases: like a jumper in one wool
